prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a nearby hand/person in frames 1–3, roughly 0.2–0.6 m from the camera, with the room’s floor and walls extending about 1–4 m away and the dark doorway/recess farther behind. The large upper-left refrigerator or cabinet is about 1–2 m away, while the partially visible person near it is farther from the foreground hand; in frame 4, the bright chair legs or narrow structure project from the lower right toward the room and partly occlude the floor. By frame 5, a person stands ahead and slightly right at roughly 2–3 m, with a smaller dark animal low and left of that person at a comparable depth; neither is within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach. Depth makes foreground separation and broad floor geometry clearer than RGB, but the near hand, object boundaries, doorway, and thin chair legs contain halos, merged surfaces, and implausibly abrupt depth changes, so metric distances are uncertain.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies a refrigerator in the upper-left region of frames 1–2, a foreground person extending partly out of the left/bottom edge in frames 1–3, a cellphone close to that person in frame 2, a small bottle near the lower-right edge of frame 2, a cat near the lower-right of frame 4, and a standing person right of centre in frame 5. The foreground person and phone are within roughly 0.2–0.7 m of the camera wearer, whereas the refrigerator is about 1–2 m away and the frame-5 person and frame-4 cat are roughly 2–3 m away; the distant person is above and right of the low animal in image coordinates. Across frames 1–3, the close person shifts from the far left toward the centre while remaining cropped and partly occluding the room; frames 4–5 reveal more open floor, then the distant person, who faces generally toward the camera wearer. The masks make object identities and partial visibility clearer than RGB, but they omit most walls, floor, doorway, furniture, and chair-like structures, inconsistently label the foreground body, and may misclassify or incompletely outline the cat, phone, bottle, and refrigerator.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates a magenta hand near the lower-left in frame 1, another near the lower-left/centre in frame 2, and another near the centre in frame 3, all roughly 0.2–0.6 m from the camera and partly cut off by the lower image boundary. Their movement from left toward centre indicates changing hand or camera orientation, but the map provides little reliable information about the rest of the nearby person because no full body skeleton is recovered. In frame 5, a yellow full-body skeleton stands right of centre about 2–3 m ahead, upright and approximately facing the camera wearer, with one arm bent and the other lower; no clear head-orientation landmarks establish definite eye contact, and no other object is shown within that person’s arm’s reach. Pose makes joint configuration and the distinction between close hands and the distant body easier to see than RGB, but frame 2 contains an isolated yellow limb-like segment, frame 4 has no detection, and missing or displaced joints make occlusion, facing direction, and exact reach estimates unreliable.
